pages.title: Getting Started
pages.content:
# Getting Started with DevForge

This guide will help you get up and running with the DevForge platform.

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.10+
- Node.js 18+
- Docker and Docker Compose
- Access to the internal Git repositories

## Development Setup

### 1. Clone the Repositories

```bash
git clone git@gitea.dev-forge.io:devforge/api-backend.git
git clone git@gitea.dev-forge.io:devforge/frontend-app.git
```

### 2. Set Up Environment

```bash
cd api-backend
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### 3. Configure Environment Variables

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in the values:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

{wikijs_getting_started}

### 4. Start the Services

```bash
docker-compose up -d
python -m uvicorn main:app --reload
```

## Next Steps

- Read the [Architecture Overview](/architecture/overview)
- Check the [API Reference](/api/reference)

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.content:
# Architecture Overview

DevForge follows a microservices architecture with the following main components.

## System Diagram

```
┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
│   Frontend  │────▶│   API GW    │────▶│  Services   │
│   (React)   │     │   (Kong)    │     │  (Python)   │
└─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘
                                               │
                    ┌─────────────┐     ┌──────┴──────┐
                    │   Redis     │◀────│  PostgreSQL │
                    │   (Cache)   │     │  (Primary)  │
                    └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘
```

## Core Services

### API Backend

The main REST API service handling:
- User authentication and authorization
- Project management
- Task tracking
- Team collaboration

### Frontend Application

React-based SPA with:
- Server-side rendering for SEO
- Real-time updates via WebSocket
- Responsive design

{wikijs_architecture}

## Data Flow

1. User requests hit the API Gateway
2. Gateway authenticates and routes to appropriate service
3. Services process requests and interact with databases
4. Responses are cached in Redis where appropriate

pages.title: API Reference
pages.content:
# API Reference

Complete reference for the DevForge REST API.

## Base URL

```
https://api.devforge.io/v1
```

## Authentication

All API requests require authentication via Bearer token:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.devforge.io/v1/users/me
```

## Endpoints

### Users

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| GET | /users/me | Get current user |
| PUT | /users/me | Update current user |
| GET | /users/:id | Get user by ID |

### Projects

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| GET | /projects | List all projects |
| POST | /projects | Create project |
| GET | /projects/:id | Get project |
| PUT | /projects/:id | Update project |
| DELETE | /projects/:id | Delete project |

{wikijs_api_reference}

### Tasks

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| GET | /projects/:id/tasks | List project tasks |
| POST | /projects/:id/tasks | Create task |
| GET | /tasks/:id | Get task |
| PUT | /tasks/:id | Update task |
| DELETE | /tasks/:id | Delete task |

## Error Responses

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "NOT_FOUND",
    "message": "Resource not found"
  }
}
```

pages.content:
# Deployment Guide

How to deploy DevForge to production environments.

## Environments

| Environment | URL | Purpose |
|-------------|-----|--------|
| Development | dev.devforge.io | Local development |
| Staging | staging.devforge.io | Pre-production testing |
| Production | devforge.io | Live environment |

## Prerequisites

- AWS CLI configured
- kubectl access to EKS cluster
- Docker registry credentials

## Deployment Process

### 1. Build and Push Images

```bash
./scripts/build.sh
docker push registry.devforge.io/api:$VERSION
docker push registry.devforge.io/frontend:$VERSION
```

### 2. Update Kubernetes Manifests

```bash
cd infrastructure/k8s
kustomize edit set image api=registry.devforge.io/api:$VERSION
```

### 3. Apply Changes

```bash
kubectl apply -k overlays/production
```

{wikijs_deployment}

## Rollback

To rollback to a previous version:

```bash
kubectl rollout undo deployment/api -n devforge
kubectl rollout undo deployment/frontend -n devforge
```

## Monitoring

Check deployment status:

```bash
kubectl get pods -n devforge
kubectl logs -f deployment/api -n devforge
```

pages.title: Runbooks
pages.content:
# Operational Runbooks

Standard procedures for common operational tasks.

## Incident Response

### High CPU Usage

1. Check which pods are affected:
   ```bash
   kubectl top pods -n devforge
   ```

2. Check recent deployments:
   ```bash
   kubectl rollout history deployment/api -n devforge
   ```

3. Scale up if needed:
   ```bash
   kubectl scale deployment/api --replicas=5 -n devforge
   ```

### Database Connection Issues

1. Verify database status:
   ```bash
   psql -h db.devforge.io -U admin -c "SELECT 1"
   ```

2. Check connection pool:
   ```sql
   SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;
   ```

3. Kill idle connections if needed:
   ```sql
   SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid)
   FROM pg_stat_activity
   WHERE state = 'idle'
   AND query_start < now() - interval '1 hour';
   ```

{wikijs_runbooks}

## Scheduled Maintenance

### Database Backups

Backups run automatically at 02:00 UTC. Manual backup:

```bash
pg_dump -h db.devforge.io -U admin devforge > backup.sql
```

### Log Rotation

Logs are rotated weekly. Force rotation:

```bash
logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/devforge
```

pages.title: Security Guidelines
pages.content:
# Security Guidelines

Security best practices for DevForge development.

## Authentication

- All endpoints must require authentication except:
  - Health checks
  - Public documentation
  - OAuth callbacks

- Use JWT with short expiry (15 min) and refresh tokens
- Store tokens securely (httpOnly cookies preferred)

## Authorization

- Implement RBAC for all resources
- Use principle of least privilege
- Validate permissions on every request

## Input Validation

- Validate all user inputs server-side
- Use parameterized queries (never string concatenation)
- Sanitize outputs to prevent XSS

{wikijs_security}

## Secrets Management

- Never commit secrets to version control
- Use AWS Secrets Manager for production secrets
- Rotate secrets quarterly
- Use different secrets per environment

## Logging

- Never log sensitive data (passwords, tokens, PII)
- Use structured logging format
- Include correlation IDs for tracing

## Reporting Security Issues

Email security@devforge.io with:
1. Description of the vulnerability
2. Steps to reproduce
3. Potential impact

Do NOT disclose publicly until patched.

pages.title: New Developer Onboarding
pages.content:
# New Developer Onboarding

Welcome to the DevForge team! Here's everything you need to get started.

## First Day Checklist

- [ ] Get access to Slack workspace
- [ ] Set up email and calendar
- [ ] Request access to:
  - [ ] GitHub organization
  - [ ] AWS Console
  - [ ] Internal tools (Jira, Confluence)

## First Week Goals

1. Complete local development setup
2. Run the full test suite
3. Review architecture documentation
4. Pair with a team member on a small task

## Development Workflow

1. Pick a task from the sprint board
2. Create a feature branch: `feature/TICKET-123-description`
3. Write code and tests
4. Create a pull request
5. Address review feedback
6. Merge after approval

{wikijs_onboarding}
